---
title: "Acquisition and real time"
---

## Acquisition to miniSEED

```bash
onthesignal acq --server 10.16.0.163 --network RD --station SN270 \
                --channels "FH?" --duration 600 --outdir data/
```

In the console: `/acq --server 10.16.0.163 --network RD --station SN270 --duration 600 --load`.

- Without `--channels`, the streams served for the station are listed (`INFO STREAMS`) and you
  choose them (`1,3` or `all`), as with the former `acq_mseed.py`.
- Progress is shown live: elapsed time, percentage, MB written, and per channel the samples
  received, the last sample time, the latency, the gaps and the effective rate.
- Records are written to disk as they arrive (`.part` files): an abrupt stop loses nothing.
  At the end, one file per channel is written (`{net}.{sta}.{loc}.{cha}_{start}.mseed`, or a
  single file when `--output` has no `{cha}`).
- **Gaps are kept**: they are detected, logged in `acquisition.log` and reported, never
  interpolated.
- Stop on the wall-clock duration (default), on the received data duration (`--data-time`),
  or on a window `--start` / `--end`. Ctrl+C stops cleanly and saves what was received.
- The connection is re-established automatically (`[seedlink] reconnect_attempts` and
  `reconnect_delay` in the configuration).
- `--load` loads the files into the session after the acquisition.

Defaults for `--server`, `--network`, `--station` can be set in the `[seedlink]` section of the
configuration.

## Real-time analysis

```bash
onthesignal rt --server 10.16.0.163 --network RD --station SN270 --channels FHZ FHN \
               --mode dsp --sensitivity 2.384e-6 --unit V
```

In the console: `/rt --server ... --channels FHZ --mode fft`.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--mode` | `stats` | `stats` (table only), `fft` or `dsp` (plus a refreshed figure) |
| `--window` | 10 s | window of the mean, standard deviation and peak-to-peak |
| `--spectral-window` | 60 s | window of the FFT / PSD |
| `--refresh`, `--plot-refresh` | 1 s, 2 s | refresh periods |
| `--record DIR` | — | also record the streams |
| `--duration` | — | stop after this time (Ctrl+C otherwise) |
